why_this_is_data_and_not_code: tests/test_architecture.py treats a string literal naming an engine as a dependency on it, because that is how the executable reaches subprocess and how an engine identity reaches a provenance row.
The retirement tooling has to keep naming both engines forever in order to prove they are absent, and #741's acceptance criterion is that the allowlist is empty.
Holding the identity here keeps one source of truth for the harness, the image audit and the retirement record, and keeps the guard's rule about source code intact.

engines.name: PyMuPDF
engines.note: One distribution supplies two importable names; the second is the historical alias most call sites use.

engines.name: Tesseract
engines.note: The Python distribution is a wrapper that shells out; the engine itself is an operating-system package, so absence has to be checked on PATH and in the package database as well as in site-packages.
